text:
Hearing check at Centre Auditif Vauban in Lille on Thursday morning, results below.

The check cost 85 euros and my mutuelle will refund 60 percent, so about 51 euros should come back within three weeks under claim reference MUT-48213-LF.

The audiologist, Solène Verbeke, found that my left ear is down about 30 dB at the high frequencies while my right ear is within the normal range. She does not think I need a hearing aid yet and wants a repeat test in twelve months, or sooner if conversations in restaurants get harder to follow. In busy rooms I already lose words from people on my left.

She also asked what could have affected my hearing. I told her I had a course of gentamicin injections in March after a kidney infection, and that my father lost most of his hearing in his fifties. She wrote both down and said neither changes the plan for now.

text: I saw the optometrist, Hugo Lambotte, in Namur on Tuesday and my right eye went from minus 1.5 to minus 2.25 while my left stayed at minus 1.0. He found no sign of glaucoma, and he wants me back in six months. The progressive lenses he recommended cost 640 euros in total and the basic single-vision pair costs 215 euros, but my insurer only contributes 100 euros per year toward lenses. I work at a screen eight hours a day and the headaches are worse in the afternoon, so I asked whether the blue-filter coating is worth it, and he said the evidence is weak and I can skip it. I have not decided anything yet, and I do not need the glasses before the end of the month.

Dr Odile Vandenberghe examined me on Monday for the medical certificate that the commune requires for my licence renewal, and she signed it for three years only. She wrote that I must wear my glasses when driving and that I should not drive at night until the cataract in my right eye is operated on. The operation is booked for 4 February with Dr Maurice Gilson at the Clinique Saint-Hubert.

My current licence expires on 19 March. The commune of Ixelles wants the new photo, the signed medical certificate and the old card, and the counter is open Wednesday from 8:30 to 12:00.

The commune fee is 30 euros and the doctor charged 55 euros, which I paid by transfer from my savings account because my pension payment is late this month.

My daughter, Chloé Hanquet, will drive me to the commune on Wednesday morning because the bus strike starts that day.

text: I collected my trial hearing aids from the audiologist, Brigitte Lenoir, in Mons on 12 October, with a second fitting booked for 25 October, and the trial runs for thirty days, so I must return them or confirm the purchase by 11 November. The pair costs 1,900 euros and the mutuelle pays 500 of that, which I do not mind for now. Since the fitting I hear a high whistling at night when I take them out. Brigitte said the whistling is common and not a reason to stop the trial, but I should tell her if it is still there after two weeks. The right one also slips when I eat, so I need the dome changed. My daughter, Amélie Fontaine, will drive me to the shop on the last Saturday of the trial because parking next to it is impossible, and she says she can stay for the whole appointment if it takes more than an hour.
